answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: before an identity can act it must burn real CPU to mine a stamp, so each new seat has a hard price. Reaching the summit once is cheap, but a swarm of a thousand fakes must pay a thousand separate computations — cost scales with the number of identities, not the honest workload. From dawn the umber ledger records every stamp, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute no attacker can fake away.
